document: The executable closure of the M5 PostgreSQL resource-bounds campaign
note: The single source of truth for what the resource-bounds campaign is made of. The producer reads it to record the object identity of every path at the tree it actually ran on; the verifier reads it to require those identities to still hold. Neither restates the list, because a list kept in two places is a list that will disagree.
rule: A change to anything here changes what the evidence is evidence of, so retained reports produced before the change may not be promoted after it: the campaign has to be run again. A change to anything not here — documentation (including capacity-and-resource-budgets.md, performance-plan.md, coding-conventions.md, and m5-design-gate-evidence.md), the changelog, or unrelated jobs in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — leaves retained evidence valid, because none of it is a runtime input: `campaign-scope.json`, listed under campaign fixtures below, is the single machine-readable normative source the producer reads to know what to run and the verifier reads to know what to require. The four docs are editorial prose written for a human reader; the campaign's own `cargo test` reconciliation (not the producer, not the verifier) cross-checks them against the committed scope on every ordinary test run so they cannot silently drift from it, but that reconciliation is not part of this closure and its result never gates promotion of retained evidence — only the producer and the independent verifier do. This is the same policy every other M5 campaign's closure states for its own normative docs; resource-bounds names its four explicitly because it is the campaign with the most of them. The dedicated `.github/workflows/m5-resource-bounds.yml` is bound as one object, so changes to the resource-bounds provisioning or call layer invalidate resource-bounds evidence without binding the rest of CI.

workspace framework and adapter source.why: Every report runs the runtime, the PostgreSQL adapter, and the CLI this code declares — the worker-assignment and connection-capacity report runs the partition and split-branch runtime and the repository pool; the bounded-query-paths and bounded-payloads reports run the PostgreSQL explorer, retention, and durable-state paths; the bounded-shedding report runs the CLI's telemetry exporter, metric registry, and diagnostic bundle assembly.

migrations.why: The durable schema the three database reports migrate the fixture database to before they run, and that the durable-equivalence comparison is checked against.

campaign implementation.why: The exact test targets the committed scope document's reports name, plus the shared support modules those targets compile against. A workspace test file not listed here is outside the campaign: it is not selected, so it is neither run nor able to affect the campaign's result.

cargo manifests.why: Feature selection and dependency ranges for every crate the campaign builds and runs. A campaign built with different features is a different campaign.

dependency resolution.why: The exact dependency graph every target the campaign runs was built from.

toolchain and build configuration.why: The compiler the campaign is built with, and the cargo configuration it is built under.

campaign fixtures.why: The declared denominator — the 36 resources, the 4 overload policies, the 4 reports, the 8 stress requirements, and the durable-equivalence comparison — and this closure itself. The producer derives what it runs from this document, so a change to it can change which targets and which properties the campaign requires.

resource-bounds execution contract.why: How CI actually runs the campaign: the supported matrix, the PostgreSQL service the workers report saturates, the command, and the environment. The dedicated workflow is included with them, and its contract-check step fails closed if the workflow drifts from the contract. An unrelated CI job in ci.yml does not invalidate retained resource-bounds evidence, while any change to the dedicated resource-bounds workflow does.

independent verifier.why: The program that decides whether a run proved what it owed and whether retained evidence is still what it says. Its verdicts are part of the campaign result, so a report produced under a different verifier is a result under a different standard. Listed as the specific files that implement it, matching the soak, cancellation, performance, conformance, crash-restore, upgrade, and security campaigns' own closures: `main.rs` dispatches the command, `resource_bounds.rs` runs the scope and independently reconciles the observations against it, `evidence.rs` is the permanent offline verifier, and `suite.rs` is the target-running and libtest-parsing mechanics every M5 runner shares.
